titulo: Menos mal / menos mal que = thank goodness
subtitulo: ¡Menos mal! Menos mal que traje paraguas.
regla: ¡Menos mal! = thank goodness, phew. Menos mal que + indicative = it's a good thing that...: Menos mal que llegaste. Never the subjunctive.

lista.texto: On its own, as a reply: _Thank goodness! Phew!_
_It's a good thing that..._, any indicative tense.

bloques.texto: Even though it's a feeling, **menos mal que** takes the **indicative**: what you're relieved about is a fact.
Tip: **menos mal** = it could have been worse.

lista.es: —Al final no va a haber paro de transporte esta semana. —¡==Menos mal==!
lista.en: —In the end there won't be a transit strike this week. —Thank goodness!

lista.es: —Tranquila, no se rompió nada en la caída. —¡==Menos mal==!
lista.en: —Don't worry, he didn't break anything when he fell. —Phew!

lista.es: —¡Encontré el anillo que había perdido! —¡==Menos mal==!
lista.en: —I found the ring I'd lost! —Thank goodness!
Thank goodness you found your ring.

lista.es: ==Menos mal que== la semana que viene tengo dos días libres.
lista.en: It's a good thing I have two days off next week.

lista.es: ==Menos mal que== traje el paraguas; si no, estaríamos empapados.
lista.en: Good thing I brought the umbrella; otherwise we'd be soaked.

lista.es: ==Menos mal que== el concierto va a ser gratis.
lista.en: Good thing the concert's going to be free.

lista.es: ==Menos mal que== la lavadora ya funciona.
lista.en: Thank goodness the washing machine works again.

lista.texto: Feelings usually take the subjunctive: [[6185|wish and feeling]].
